hero.caption: The relationship is yours and theirs — no one else is ever in the room.
hero.variant.a.headline: Your contact card. Your channels. Your rules.
hero.variant.a.label: Permission-first
hero.variant.a.sub: Give each person the right door, and close it to future updates anytime. What they already saw stays with them.
hero.variant.b.headline: No brainrot. No feeds. Just people.
hero.variant.b.label: The anti-feed
hero.variant.b.sub: No feed to scroll, no ads, no tracking. Vauchi is built to know as little about you as it can, and to stay that way.
hero.variant.c.headline: Connect on your own terms, on the channels you choose.
hero.variant.c.label: Built for everyone
hero.variant.c.sub: Choose which numbers and handles each person sees. When you change one, they get it the next time their app syncs.
hero.variant.d.headline: Exchange contacts, not access to your life.
hero.variant.d.label: Reframed privacy
hero.variant.d.sub: Share work details with colleagues and personal ones with friends, all from one card.
hero.variant.e.headline: Stop renting your address book.
hero.variant.e.label: Anti-adtech
hero.variant.e.sub: On a platform, your contacts last as long as your account. Vauchi keeps them on your own devices, with no account to lose and no ads to feed.
hero.variant.f.headline: Meet once. Stay in touch.
hero.variant.f.label: Stay in touch
hero.variant.f.sub: Exchange in person or by link and code. Your details reach them on their next sync — no accounts, no feeds.
hero.variant.g.headline: The address book that fixes itself.
hero.variant.g.label: Silent updates
hero.variant.g.sub: When a contact changes their number, the new one reaches you the next time your phone syncs. End-to-end encrypted, and open source.
hero.variant.h.headline: Stay reachable. On your own terms.
hero.variant.h.label: Own your reachability
hero.variant.h.sub: Your number, inbox and job will change. Change them once in Vauchi, and the people you chose get the update when their app syncs.
hero.variant.i.headline: Nobody but you should own the way you can be reached.
hero.variant.i.label: Owned by you
hero.variant.i.sub: That belief shapes every choice: no account, no platform to join, and a relay that can't read your card. Our goal is for independent operators to run it.
honest.heading: What Vauchi does not do
honest.item1: It does not take back what you already shared. You choose what each person sees, and you can change it or withdraw it at any time — but someone who has already read your number can remember it. Nobody can unsend.
honest.item2: It is not protection from someone dangerous. Vauchi can stop sending someone updates, quietly. It cannot make you unfindable, and we will not pretend otherwise.
honest.item3: It is not finished. Vauchi is being built in the open and the apps are not out yet. Everything here describes what we are building — and the code is public, so you can check how far it has come.
honest.item4: There is still a server in the middle. Your phone can't keep an open line to everyone you know — that would drain the battery — so updates wait at a relay until your phone next checks in. The relay holds them sealed and has no key, and the addresses it sorts by change every day, so it is never handed the list of who knows whom. It does see that something arrived. You can run your own.
honest.label: Being straight with you
honest.note: If anything on this page ever stops matching the code, the code is the truth.

why.body1: The internet handed everyone a permanent address — a number, an inbox, a profile — and then made it expensive to leave. Change one and you spend a year chasing the people who matter. Keep it, and it follows you for the rest of your life.
why.body2: People change jobs, countries, phones and names. The way we reach each other should be allowed to change too — without asking a company for permission, and without losing anyone along the way.
why.heading: Contact details were never meant to be permanent.

whypage.index.title: Why Vauchi
whypage.index.description: Reasons to choose Vauchi, each with its limits: nobody can look you up, you can change your number once, and it is not a social network.
whypage.index.heading: Why Vauchi
whypage.index.intro: Each page below explains one reason to use Vauchi: what it protects, and where it stops.
whypage.no-directory.title: Nobody can look you up: contact sharing with no directory
whypage.no-directory.description: Vauchi has no public directory, no search and no inbox. Your details reach only people you swapped cards with. What that stops, and what it cannot.
whypage.no-directory.heading: Nobody can look you up
whypage.no-directory.intro1: Most apps that hold your contact details also let strangers find you: a search by phone number, a username, a list of people you may know. Vauchi has none of these. There is no directory to search and no profile to find.
whypage.no-directory.intro2: That stops strangers from reaching you through Vauchi. It does not stop spam on the phone number or email address you share, because Vauchi does not control those.
whypage.no-directory.s1.heading: People get your card only from you
whypage.no-directory.s1.body: Someone gets your contact card only when the two of you exchange it: in person, by scanning each other's QR codes, or remotely, with a link and a code that you send them yourself. Nobody can request your card, search for you, or be suggested to you.
whypage.no-directory.s2.heading: There is no inbox to spam
whypage.no-directory.s2.body: Vauchi is not a messenger. It carries contact details, not messages, so there is nothing in it for anyone to fill with spam. People reach you through the number, address or handle you chose to share with them.
whypage.no-directory.s3.heading: You decide what each person sees
whypage.no-directory.s3.body: Each detail on your card is shown to or hidden from every contact separately, and a new detail starts hidden from everyone. A colleague can have your work email without ever seeing your private number.
whypage.no-directory.s4.heading: Leaving a spammed number costs you nothing
whypage.no-directory.s4.body: If a number or address starts attracting spam, switch to a new one and change it on your card. The people you shared it with get the new one automatically, so dropping the old one does not cut you off from the people you know.
whypage.no-directory.limit1: It cannot stop spam that arrives by phone, text or email. A number you share can still be leaked, guessed or sold by someone else.
whypage.no-directory.limit2: A contact can copy what you show them, and many apps upload whole address books. Hiding a detail later stops future updates; it cannot take back a copy.
whypage.no-directory.limit3: Updates pass through a relay, a server that holds them until the other phone collects them. It cannot read them, but it sees that something was sent, when, and roughly how big.
whypage.no-directory.q1: Can someone find me on Vauchi with my phone number?
whypage.no-directory.a1: No. Vauchi has no search, by phone number or anything else. People get your card only by exchanging it with you.
whypage.no-directory.a2: Not directly. Spam arrives on your phone line or email, which Vauchi does not control. What Vauchi changes is the cost of escaping it: move to a new number, and the people you know get it without you telling each of them.
whypage.no-directory.q3: Can a stranger send me a message through Vauchi?
whypage.no-directory.a3: No. Vauchi carries contact details, not messages, and only between people who exchanged cards.
whypage.change-your-number.title: Change your number without telling everyone
whypage.change-your-number.description: Change your phone number, email or handle once in Vauchi, and everyone who holds your card gets it. How it works, what it needs, and what it can't undo.
whypage.change-your-number.heading: Change your number without telling everyone
whypage.change-your-number.intro1: A new phone number usually means a group message to everyone you know, and months of people trying the old one. With Vauchi you change it once, on your own card, and the people who hold your card get the new number automatically.
whypage.change-your-number.intro2: They get it the next time their app goes online, not instantly, and only if you let them see that detail.
whypage.change-your-number.s1.heading: How it works
whypage.change-your-number.s1.body: When you exchange cards with someone, your two phones set up a private channel between you. Change a detail on your card, and Vauchi sends the change to every contact allowed to see it. Only the two of you can read it, not the relay in between and not the people who run it.
whypage.change-your-number.s2.heading: What you can change
whypage.change-your-number.s2.body: Anything on your card: phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, and social or messaging handles. Edit a detail, and its new value goes to everyone who can see it. Add a new one, and it starts hidden: only the people you choose for it receive it.
whypage.change-your-number.s3.heading: Who gets the update
whypage.change-your-number.s3.body: Each contact gets only the details you let them see. Change your private number, and only the people who can see that number get the new one. Everyone else's view of your card stays as it was.
whypage.change-your-number.s4.heading: When it arrives
whypage.change-your-number.s4.body: Updates wait on a relay, a server that holds sealed updates until the other phone next goes online, so neither phone has to stay awake waiting for the other. A contact who is offline for weeks gets the change when they reconnect, within 120 days.
whypage.change-your-number.limit1: Vauchi does not detect a new number for you. You change the detail on your card yourself, and that change is what your contacts receive.
whypage.change-your-number.limit2: It updates your card in Vauchi. A copy someone saved elsewhere, such as their phone's address book or a screenshot, keeps the old details.
whypage.change-your-number.limit3: The relay cannot read the update, but it sees that something was sent, when, and roughly how big.
whypage.change-your-number.q1: Do my contacts need to do anything?
whypage.change-your-number.a1: No. Once you have exchanged cards, updates reach them the next time their app syncs, for example when they open it.
whypage.change-your-number.q2: What if I change my number while a contact's phone is off?
whypage.change-your-number.a2: The update waits, sealed, until their phone reconnects, for up to 120 days.
whypage.change-your-number.q3: Can I keep someone from getting my new number?
whypage.change-your-number.a3: Yes. Hide that detail from them before you change it, and they get no further changes to it. If you use several devices, let them sync first.
whypage.beyond-social-network.title: Beyond the social network: your identity and contacts stay yours
whypage.beyond-social-network.descriptio: Vauchi is not a social network. The people you know stay with you when a platform closes, updates are sealed end to end, and trust comes from meeting.
whypage.beyond-social-network.heading: Beyond the social network
whypage.beyond-social-network.intro1: The people you know are spread across platforms: a number here, a handle on Instagram, a profile on LinkedIn. Each platform holds its piece of your life as an account on its servers. When one closes, changes its rules, or you simply leave, the people you reached there can be lost with it.
whypage.beyond-social-network.intro2: Vauchi keeps the people you know on your phone, with every way to reach them. There is no account and no feed, and the updates between you are sealed so that we cannot read them. It is not another social network: it is a living address book, and the part a social network should never have owned.
whypage.beyond-social-network.s1.heading: Your identity is a key on your phone, not an account
whypage.beyond-social-network.s1.body: Vauchi has no sign-up, no username and no account to log in to. When you start, your phone creates your identity: a pair of keys that stays on your devices, plus any backup you choose to make, sealed with your password. No company can suspend it, rename it or sell it.
whypage.beyond-social-network.s2.heading: When a platform goes, the people you know stay
whypage.beyond-social-network.s2.body: The people you exchanged cards with are a list on your phone, not on our servers, and each card holds every way to reach that person. If a platform you use closes, or you leave it, change that detail once on your card, and everyone you let see it gets the new one. You can also back the list up into a file only you can open, or export it as standard contact cards (vCard).
whypage.beyond-social-network.s3.heading: Privacy is how it is built, not a setting
whypage.beyond-social-network.s3.body: Every update to a contact is sealed on your phone before it leaves, so only the two of you can read it — not the relay that carries it, not us. There is no switch that turns this off, and the app has no ads, trackers or analytics. The relay still sees that something was sent, roughly when, and roughly how big.
whypage.beyond-social-network.s4.heading: Trust comes from meeting, not from a badge
whypage.beyond-social-network.s4.body: On a social network, a blue check or a follower count suggests who to trust. In Vauchi you swap cards face to face by scanning each other's codes, and the card remembers how you exchanged — in person or by link. Nobody can edit that, including us.
whypage.beyond-social-network.limit1: Vauchi does not replace a social network. There is no feed, no posts and no chat: it keeps contact details current, and you talk through the channels on each card.
whypage.beyond-social-network.limit2: Updates travel through a relay we run, behind a privacy hop that hides your IP address from it. Today we run that hop as well, so the two are not yet independent.
whypage.beyond-social-network.limit3: Your identity lives on your devices. Lose your phone with no backup, no second device and no recovery contacts, and nobody can give it back, including us: there is no password reset.
whypage.beyond-social-network.a1: No. It has no feed, no followers, no posts and no messages. It carries contact details between people who exchanged cards, and keeps them up to date.
whypage.beyond-social-network.q2: What happens if a platform I use shuts down?
whypage.beyond-social-network.a2: The people you exchanged cards with are in Vauchi, not on that platform. Change the handle or number on your card once, and everyone you let see it gets the new one.
whypage.beyond-social-network.q3: Can Vauchi see who I know?
whypage.beyond-social-network.a3: It is never told: there is no account, and the relay routes sealed updates by codes that change daily and mean nothing on their own. It can still see which codes receive updates, when, and roughly how big. Hiding that too is on our public roadmap.

support.heading: Support Vauchi
support.intro: Vauchi is free and open source. Donations pay for its development and for the servers it runs on.
support.platforms.heading: Donation platforms
support.bank: Bank transfer in CHF or EUR: email us for the account details
support.crypto.heading: Bitcoin and Monero
support.crypto.intro: Scan a code with your wallet, or copy an address. Before you send, check that the address in your wallet matches the one on this page. If you send straight from an exchange, the exchange knows you donated to Vauchi.
support.bitcoin-silent-payments.heading: Bitcoin: Silent Payments
support.bitcoin-silent-payments.note: Each payment goes to a new address on the blockchain, so the blockchain alone does not show that it went to Vauchi. Your wallet needs to support Silent Payments (the BIP-352 standard). If it rejects this address, use the one below.
support.bitcoin-silent-payments.qr_alt: QR code of the Bitcoin Silent Payments address
support.bitcoin.heading: Bitcoin: standard address
support.bitcoin.note: Works with most current Bitcoin wallets. Payments to this address are public: anyone can see each payment, its amount and the address it came from.
support.bitcoin.qr_alt: QR code of the standard Bitcoin address
support.monero.heading: Monero
support.monero.note: Monero hides the amount and the receiving address of each payment, and hides the sender among other users' payments.
